steps: Assess for rapidly progressive GN (rising creatinine) — nephrology emergency; urgent biopsy.
Send immunology (ANCA, anti-GBM, complement, ANA) before immunosuppression.
RPGN: high-dose corticosteroids + cyclophosphamide/rituximab ± plasma exchange (anti-GBM/severe).
Supportive: BP control (ACEi/ARB), manage fluid/electrolytes, treat any infection trigger.
Treat the specific cause; monitor renal function closely.

drugRefs.dose: 500–1000 mg once daily for 3 days, then oral prednisolone ~1 mg/kg/day (max ~60–80 mg) tapering
drugRefs.freq: pulse x3 days, then daily oral taper
drugRefs.why: Rapid suppression of glomerular inflammation in RPGN/crescentic GN. Specialist-directed.

drugRefs.dose: IV 15 mg/kg (max 1.2 g) every 2–3 weeks, or oral 2 mg/kg/day (reduce for age/renal function)
drugRefs.why: Induction immunosuppression for ANCA-associated and anti-GBM crescentic GN. Specialist-directed with PJP prophylaxis.

drugRefs.dose: 375 mg/m² IV weekly for 4 weeks (or 1 g IV x2, 2 weeks apart)
drugRefs.why: Alternative induction agent for ANCA-associated GN, especially where cyclophosphamide is undesirable. Specialist-directed.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Glomerular Diseases
KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases

drugRefs.dose: start 2.5 mg once daily, titrate to 10 mg as tolerated
drugRefs.why: Reduces proteinuria and controls blood pressure. Monitor potassium and creatinine; an ARB is an alternative if ACEi not tolerated.

confirm: Haematuria (dysmorphic RBCs/casts), proteinuria, hypertension ± AKI. Rapidly progressive GN is an emergency.
